DEEPAK NITRITE Q1: MANAGEMENT SEES STRONG GROWTH AS GLOBAL CHEMICAL SUPPLY CHAINS SHIFT 🧪🌍

• 🌏 Global chemical industry is shifting towards resilient, regionally diversified supply chains, creating a long-term opportunity for India

• ⚙️ Deepak Nitrite delivered strong Q1 performance through proactive raw material sourcing, inventory planning, uninterrupted operations and operational excellence

• 🔗 Integrated value chains, downstream expansion, long-term feedstock partnerships and advanced materials investments are strengthening earnings quality and resilience

• 📈 Management sees improving demand visibility across domestic and export markets, supported by new product launches, capacity additions and stronger downstream demand

• 🚀 Confident of sustaining growth by remaining agile amid global volatility and strengthening India's position as a global chemicals manufacturing hub

DEEPAK NITRITE Q1: POLYCARBONATE PROJECT ADVANCES ACROSS KEY MILESTONES 🏗️🧪

• 🇩🇪 Plant dismantling at Stade, Germany is progressing well, with equipment shipments already reaching the Dahej site

• 🇮🇳 Civil infrastructure work has commenced in India after contractor mobilization

• ⚙️ Ordering for major OSBL equipment has been completed, with total project commitment at around ₹2,900 crore

• 🔋 Signed a long-term agreement for a dedicated HyCO plant to ensure reliable raw material supply, improve operational efficiency and strengthen supply chain security

• 🎯 Polycarbonate project and HyCO facility remain on track for 2028 commissioning

DEEPAK NITRITE Q1: PHENOLICS HIT RECORD PERFORMANCE; ADVANCED INTERMEDIATES OUTLOOK REMAINS STRONG 🧪📈

• 🏭 Phenolics delivered its highest-ever quarterly performance with ₹1,775 Cr revenue and ₹418 Cr EBIT, driven by favourable spreads and strong domestic realizations

• ⚙️ High operating rates maintained through proactive feedstock management and stable demand across key products

• 📈 Profitability improved through process optimisation, debottlenecking, disciplined commercial execution and strategic benzene sourcing

• 🚀 Advanced Intermediates saw sequential improvement, supported by better realizations, proactive procurement and strong performance across key products

• 🌱 Growth outlook remains positive with debottlenecking, new product additions, nitric acid, nitration & hydrogenation products, and upcoming specialty agrochemical & multipurpose plants

DEEPAK NITRITE Q1: STRONG START TO FY27 WITH ROBUST GROWTH DESPITE VOLATILE MARKET CONDITIONS 

• 📈 Delivered strong revenue and profitability growth despite a volatile operating environment

• 🌍 Successfully navigated geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions and feedstock price volatility through proactive procurement and supply chain management

• ⚙️ Performance supported by integrated operations, steady capacity utilisation, favourable product mix and recent integration initiatives

• ⚡ Continued focus on operational excellence, yield improvement, energy optimisation and commercialisation of new products enhanced earnings quality

• 🚀 Management remains optimistic on growth, backed by improving demand visibility, downstream capacity expansion and a strong new product pipeline

🟢 Impact: Positive (Strong execution, operational resilience and expansion initiatives support sustained growth outlook.)

The biggest beneficiaries of the Closing Auction Session were Arbitrage Funds and this is visible in the change of fund NAVs on 3rd August 

Arbitrage funds recorded their highest daily return (~0.50%) in history by delivering 8–10 times their average daily returns (~0.05%)

UTI Arbitrage Fund : +0.40%

Nippon India Arb Fund : +0.48%
Invesco Arbitrage Fund : +0.42%

7 of 10 funds recorded their highest daily percentage gain in the last decade on the first day of the Closing Auction Session

These funds saw a very rare rise in their net asset values across the category, averaging 0.46%. This was about 7.3 standard deviations higher than their usual daily movement

Arbitrage funds are mutual funds that make money by buying a stock cheaply in the cash market and selling it at a higher price in the derivatives (futures) market at the same time

AVALON TECH Q1 ; Q1 FY27 delivers eighth consecutive quarter of sequential improvement in performance

India manufacturing delivered 16.7% EBITDA & 11.1% PAT in Q1 FY27

Net Working Capital days improved from 142 days in Jun'25 to 117 days in Jun'26

Order book increased by 23.4% YoY

Brownfield expansion for domestic demand (Chennai) is operational

Secured EN 15085-2 certification, strengthening our capabilities in railway welding applications

AVALON TECHNOLOGIES Q1: OUTLINES LONG-TERM GROWTH STRATEGY 🚀🔧

• 🌍 Leveraging the India–US manufacturing model to capitalise on global EMS opportunities, with India as the primary manufacturing hub

• 🤝 Focused on strengthening customer relationships through upselling, cross-selling and deeper collaboration

• ⚡ Expanding into next-generation technologies, including partnerships with clean energy technology companies

• 📈 Maintaining a balanced strategy focused on profitable growth, targeting high-value sectors such as aerospace and other complex industrial products

• 🏗️ Aiming to move up the value chain by strengthening design-led engineering capabilities alongside manufacturing

WELSPUN ENTERPRISES Q1: STRONG ORDER BOOK, CAPITAL RECYCLING GAINS MOMENTUM 🚧📈

• 📊 Q1 revenue stood at ₹774 crore with a healthy EBITDA margin of 22.9%; order book remained strong at ₹18,729 crore

• 💰 Signed a definitive agreement to divest the Aunta–Simaria road asset at an enterprise value of around ₹1,000 crore, advancing its capital recycling strategy

• 🚇 Received all regulatory clearances for the Dharavi–Ghatkopar Tunnel Project, enabling faster construction

• 🛣️ Executed the Sub-Concession Agreement for the Pune–Shirur Road Project

• 💵 Consolidated cash & cash equivalents stood at ₹1,792 crore as of June 30, 2026, supporting future growth

• 🚀 Management remains confident of delivering medium-term growth, backed by a robust order book, healthy balance sheet and strong bid pipeline

METRO BRANDS Q1: NEW BRANDS & FORMAT EXPANSION UPDATE 👟🚀

• 👠 Clarks Cloudsteppers women's range now available in ~300 MBOs, while the men's range is present in ~100 MBOs

• 📦 Full Clarks product range expected by Q2 FY27; Clarks EBOs planned for Q3 FY27 after supply chain stabilisation

• ⚠️ Foot Locker & MetroActiv store expansion remains cautious due to BIS-related supply chain challenges affecting select global brands

• 🇮🇳 Fila has started local footwear manufacturing in India to address BIS-related issues, while brand repositioning is underway

• 🏬 Opened 1 Fila EBO in Vizag and 1 New Era EBO in Mumbai during the quarter

METRO BRANDS Q1: WEDDING SEASON DRIVES GROWTH, STORE EXPANSION CONTINUES 👞📈

• 💍 Strong Q1 growth driven by wedding season demand and improving consumer sentiment from mid-June; April-May remained subdued due to the US-Iran conflict overhang and Adhik Maas

• 🏬 Added 13 new stores during the quarter, while 4 stores were closed

• 🛒 E-commerce (including omni-channel) sales grew 9% YoY, contributing 13.1% of revenue

• 📢 PAT margins were impacted by higher investments in talent, brand-building, increased occupancy costs from new formats and lower treasury income

RASHI PERIPHERALS Q1: OUTLINES LONG-TERM GROWTH STRATEGY 🚀💻

• 🤝 Strengthening strategic OEM partnerships with leading global technology brands to expand offerings

• 📈 Expanding into high-growth technology verticals to diversify revenue streams

• 🌍 Accelerating market penetration through expansion into new geographies while deepening presence in existing markets

• 🖥️ Entering adjacent product segments to leverage its established distribution and channel network

• 💼 Driving solution-based selling to increase cross-selling, upselling and wallet share per partner

RASHI PERIPHERALS Q1: RECORD OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE, EXPANDS AI & ENTERPRISE CAPABILITIES 🚀💻

• 📈 Delivered record quarterly operational performance, driven by growth in enterprise solutions, distribution and strategic technology partnerships

• 🤝 Invested in VDA Infosolutions, strengthening managed IT services, solution implementation and lifecycle support through forward integration

• 🧠 Partnered with WEKA.io to expand capabilities in AI infrastructure and high-performance workload management

• 📍 Expanded Tier-2 footprint with new branches in Udaipur (Rajasthan) and Dhule (Maharashtra), enhancing customer reach

• 🌐 Continued to strengthen its enterprise solutions portfolio and distribution network across high-growth markets

VENTIVE HOSPITALITY: APPROVES MERGER OF TWO SUBSIDIARIES 🔄🏨

• 🏢 Board approved the merger of Sun Leisure (India) Pvt. Ltd. with Soham Leisure Ventures Pvt. Ltd. through a Scheme of Amalgamation

• 📌 Sun Leisure is a wholly owned subsidiary of Soham Leisure, while Soham Leisure is a subsidiary of Ventive Hospitality

• ⚙️ Merger aims to consolidate hospitality operations, improve resource utilisation and streamline management

• 📈 Expected to create a stronger operational platform, enhance efficiency and provide a more investor-friendly corporate structure

• 💰 No cash consideration or share exchange involved as part of the merger

🟢 Impact: Neutral to Positive (Internal restructuring simplifies the group structure and may improve operational efficiency.)

VIVIANA POWER Q1: FOCUSED RESTRUCTURING, STRONG EXECUTION DRIVES GROWTH ⚡📈

• 🚀 Q1 revenue surged 246% YoY to ₹71.86 crore, while EBITDA (+232%) and PAT (+232%) rose to ₹11.56 crore and ₹6.93 crore, respectively

• 💹 EBITDA margin stood at 16.08% and PAT margin at 9.65%, supported by disciplined project execution and operational efficiency

• ⚡ Strategic restructuring to sharpen focus on core power infrastructure, including EPC, transmission & distribution, transformer manufacturing, renewable energy and BESS

• 🏭 Integration of transformer manufacturing within the company to improve operational control, execution capabilities and value-chain synergies

• 📊 Restructuring aims to simplify the corporate structure, optimise capital allocation, improve management accountability and enhance investor transparency

• 📦 Healthy order book and strong bidding pipeline provide confidence in sustaining growth momentum

PNB HOUSING Q1: STRONG LOAN GROWTH, ASSET QUALITY REMAINS HEALTHY 🏦📈

• 💰 Disbursements rose 56% YoY on cheque handover basis; reported disbursements grew 18% YoY under the new cheque realisation-based recognition

• 📊 Retail loan book increased 16% YoY to ₹89,178 crore, while total loan book grew 15% YoY to ₹89,670 crore

• 🤝 Completed a ₹146 crore pool buyout in Q1 FY27 to support faster loan growth

• 📉 Spread remained stable at 2.12%; NIM moderated 19 bps QoQ due to higher leverage and Q4 true-up impact

• ✅ Asset quality stayed strong with GNPA at 0.95% (vs 0.93% QoQ); recovered ₹67 crore from written-off accounts during the quarter

• 🛡️ July'26 fraud relates to a legacy account fully written off in FY23, with no financial impact

PNB HOUSING: ACCELERATES AI-LED DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION 🤖🏦

• 🚀 Roadmap to evolve from GenAI pilots to a full Agentic AI enterprise, with AI embedded across core workflows

• 🤖 AI use cases include SUD calling, Pre-delinquency AI, Top-up AI, Re-KYC AI, PD AI Assistant, RO Copilot and grievance redressal bots

• 📞 AI voice initiatives are delivering better customer engagement, with SUD AI Calling and Pre-Delinquency AI Calling already live

• 📲 Digital onboarding enables paperless, end-to-end remote processing, reducing turnaround time, costs and improving compliance

• 🎯 Long-term vision includes autonomous AI agents, multi-agent orchestration, self-learning systems and human-in-the-loop governance

GANESH CONSUMER Q1: EXPANDS INTO NEW FOOD CATEGORIES 🚀🍘

• 🍿 Preparing a wider rollout of its ethnic snacks portfolio later in FY27 after a successful soft launch

• 🍬 Plans to launch packaged sweets and the full ethnic snacks range in Q3 FY27 from its Amta manufacturing unit

• 🌱 Commenced distribution of Soya Chunks, expanding its value-added, protein-led food portfolio

• 🏭 Leveraging existing manufacturing infrastructure to drive growth in adjacent food categories

• 📈 Focused on strengthening core business, scaling value-added products and expanding presence across existing and new markets

GANESH CONSUMER Q1: MARGIN EXPANSION DESPITE DEMAND HEADWINDS 🌾📈

• 📉 Total income declined 6.8% YoY due to heatwave, LPG supply constraints and election-related disruptions

• 🛒 B2C revenue fell 4.1% YoY, while B2B declined 17.9% YoY as the company reduced lower-margin B2B business

• 📊 Gained 1 percentage point each in market share and weighted distribution, strengthening brand presence

• 💹 EBITDA margin expanded to a record 11.2%, up 66 bps YoY and 313 bps QoQ, driven by better product mix and cost optimisation

• 💰 PAT grew 31.4% YoY to ₹12.5 crore, with PAT margin improving to 6.6%, despite higher advertising spends

PONDY OXIDES Q1: OUTLINES STRONG LONG-TERM GROWTH DRIVERS 🚀♻️

• 🏭 Capacity expansion across existing businesses with diversification into Lithium-ion and forward integration

• 💰 Strong capex pipeline backed by a balanced mix of debt, equity and internal accruals

• 🇮🇳 Stricter BWMR & EPR regulations expected to improve domestic scrap availability

• 🤝 Open to M&A, joint ventures and strategic collaborations to accelerate growth

• ⚙️ Focused on improving operational efficiency through technology and automation to enhance margins

🟢 Impact: Positive (Expansion, value addition, regulatory tailwinds and efficiency initiatives support long-term growth.)

PONDY OXIDES Q1: STRONG GROWTH BACKED BY VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS ♻️📈

• 💰 Standalone revenue rose 56% YoY to ₹931 crore; EBITDA increased 30% to ₹55.9 crore and PAT grew 32% to ₹36.3 crore

• 🟠 Copper production and sales surged over 3x YoY, while lead volumes were strategically moderated to focus on higher-margin products

• 📊 Achieved highest-ever Lead EBITDA of ₹21,595 per ton, up 28% YoY

• 🏭 Incurred ₹5 crore capex in Q1; plans to invest an additional ₹175 crore during FY27

• ⚙️ Lead capacity expanded over 50% to 2.04 lakh MTPA, with the new 72,000 MTPA capacity ramping up towards 70% utilisation

• 🔧 Investing ₹200 crore to establish a 36,000 MTPA LME Grade A Copper Cathode facility, with Phase I (18,000 MTPA) targeted for commissioning by December 2026

PONDY OXIDES Q1: MANAGEMENT CONFIDENT ON TARGET 2030 🎯♻️

• 📈 Q1FY27 revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 56%, 30% and 32% YoY, driven by better realizations and a richer value-added product mix

• 🟠 Copper business maintained strong momentum, with sales increasing over 3.5x YoY

• 🔋 Lead volumes were moderated strategically to prioritize value-added products, resulting in a record Lead EBITDA of ₹21,595/ton, up 28% YoY

• 🏭 Company remains on track for its Target 2030 vision, supported by lead and copper capacity expansions and forward integration initiatives

• 🌱 Continued focus on operational excellence, sustainability and value-added products is expected to drive profitable long-term growth

UBL Q1: MANAGEMENT REMAINS BULLISH ON LONG-TERM GROWTH 🍺📈

• 🇮🇳 Management sees strong long-term growth potential for the Indian beer industry, driven by premiumisation, favourable demographics and rising beer consumption

• 🌟 UBL will continue to strengthen its portfolio through innovation and premium offerings

• ⚙️ Focus remains on improving productivity, cost efficiency and operational excellence

• 🤝 Company will continue advocating for policy reforms to support sustainable growth of the beer industry

• 🎯 With disciplined capital allocation and a focus on profitable growth, UBL believes it is well-positioned to capture future opportunities

UBL Q1 : CEO Says This has been a historic quarter for the industry as the beer revolution has started in India. 

Karnataka is leading with an ABV based tax reform and Maharashtra, Jharkhand and Andhra Pradesh continue to see significant category growth driven by policy reforms. 

We are delighted to continue playing our leadership role as category maker through strong brands, effective advocacy and disciplined execution. 

We expect inflationary pressures on our cost base to persist over the coming quarters amid an uncertain macroeconomic environment.

 As such, we remain focused on disciplined pricing, rigorous cost management and driving productivity to protect margins while continuing to invest in the long- term growth of the business.

UNITED BREWERIES (UBL) Q1: PREMIUM BEER & CASH FLOW STRENGTH DRIVE PERFORMANCE 🍺📈

• 🍺 Beer category maintained double-digit growth; sell-in volumes rose 9%, while sell-out volumes increased 13%

• 💰 Net sales grew 7%, driven by volume growth, price hikes and favourable geographic mix

• 🌟 Premium volumes rose 17% (excluding two states); Heineken Silver volumes jumped 28% and Kingfisher Ultra grew 11%

• 📊 EBITDA margin improved to 10.9% from 6.5% in the previous quarter despite Middle East war-related cost pressures

• 💵 Free operating cash flow surged 38% to ₹548 crore, supported by disciplined working capital management

• 🏭 Commissioned a new canning line in Telangana; expansion projects in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh remain on track, while Ludhiana brewery closure supports North Grid optimisation

Unimech Aerospace's micro gas turbine engine story, a closer look:

1. Unimech Aerospace is a precision engineering and manufacturing company serving Aerospace, Defence, Semiconductors and Energy. It does not design engines itself.
Instead, the engine IP sits with its associate, Dheya Engineering Technologies, while Unimech has exclusive manufacturing rights for its aero-engine products.

2. In December 2025, Unimech increased its stake in Dheya from 17% to 30%. This isn't a passive investment, it's a strategic design-to-manufacturing partnership

3. Dheya's product lineup:
→ DET 500: India's first indigenously designed 500N-class micro turbojet
→ DET 60: Hydrogen flex-fuel micro turbogenerator
→ Modular turbojet family, scalable 200N to 3,500N
→ ATAL: tabletop aero-engine lab for training/R&D
→ Oil-free hydrogen recirculation systems for naval use

4. Target applications: UAVs, target drones, loitering munitions, distributed power, naval propulsion.

5. Technical progress: a 65,000 RPM bench test milestone was hit (disclosed in Q3 FY26 investor presentation, Feb 2026).

6. Dheya's ownership and funding trail:
→ ₹2.5cr pre-seed from iHub DivyaSampark (2023)
→ ₹10.5cr from Unimech (2024)
→ Unimech's stake raised from 17% to 30% (Dec 2025)

**Sedemac Mechatronics - R&D-led growth story
**
Sedemac’s journey started with sensor-less commutation (SLC) - its key technology moat that helped it scale rapidly in 2W/3W starter generators. Now, the same R&D engine is being leveraged to build the next layers of growth.

1. Core business still has runway: ISG penetration could rise from 40-45% → 55-60%, while Sedemac’s market share could expand from 36-38% → 46-48% by FY29.

2. EVs become the next growth engine: Its e2W/e3W motor controllers are expected to grow at a massive ~75% CAGR, potentially reaching 10-12% market share by FY29.

3. New growth layers are getting added: Sedemac is entering power tools, LCVs, CV after-treatment & EFI systems, while its genset business (~75% market share) continues to scale.

4. Capacity is being built ahead of demand: With existing plants at >90% utilisation, two new facilities should triple capacity, while Chennai land provides further expansion optionality.

HSBC expects FY26-29 Revenue / EBITDA / PAT CAGR of ~32% / 35% / 49%, with ROCE improving to ~29%.

The backbone remains R&D (~7% of revenue) allowing Sedemac to repeatedly build new products around its core technology.

Aimtron : Initiation of coverage by Nuvama (31 July 2026)

AIMTRON focuses on high-value, niche markets, and specialty businesses rather than competing in high-volume, low-margin segments. Its focus has been on critical nature industries in the industrial EMS segment as it evolves from a pure play PCB assembler to a box-build and original design manufacturer.

AIMTRON operates in the industrial B2B EMS space, where lower volumes are offset by better pricing given the complex, safety-critical, and customised nature of products, as reflected in its industry-leading margin and returns. Despite delivering the fastest growth vis-à-vis its peers, it trades cheaper at 17.3x FY28E EV/EBITDA and 27.2x P/E. The stock currently trades at a significant discount to its B2B ESDM peer set which we believe will close as the company scales. We initiate with a ‘BUY’ rating valuing the company at 40x FY28E diluted EPS of INR 50.9 resulting in a target price of INR 2,036.

AIC acquisition to bolster US presence : 

The acquisition provides AIMTRON with four SMT lines, with end-to-end capabilities, in a 58,000 sq. ft. manufacturing facility. It also has 3.9 acres of land available for future expansion. AIC’s expertise lies in high-reliability electronics, ruggedised products, and box-build manufacturing. The facility is close to major industrial OEMs such as Caterpillar, Deere & Company, CNH Industrial, and Bunn-O-Matic Corporation, thus providing a much faster route to expanding its US manufacturing footprint than building a greenfield facility.

AIC generated USD16.9mn (~INR160cr) of revenue in CY2025 and contributed USD1.6mn (~INR15cr) to the group's consolidated revenue during its first two months of consolidation in FY26 (February–March). During this period, its revenue was primarily driven by ruggedised electronics (26%), meditech (19%), BESS (17.8%), and defence (17.1%), highlighting strong strategic alignment with AIMTRON's core business. From a product mix perspective, PCBA/box-build solutions accounted for 64.9%/35.1% of revenue.

The management expects utilisation to scale to 90% from 54%, increasing its annual revenue potential to USD25–30mn (INR280–300cr) over the next three years. While AIC operated at an EBITDA margin of ~11% at the time of its acquisition, it expects to quickly ramp up to standalone margin levels within two years and expects the business to be EPS accretive from the first year.

Greenfield expansion to enhance ESDM positioning

The new facility will add six SMT lines in a phased manner and will also house a dedicated ODM, R&D, and defence zone to strengthen its engineering and high-precision manufacturing capabilities.

The project is being funded through preferential warrants (INR94.6cr) and internal accruals. The facility is expected to turn operational in phases from Q3 or Q4FY27, with the commissioning of the SMT line targeted by Q4FY27 or Q1FY28. On completion, the expansion is expected to potentially add ~INR500cr of annual revenue to the existing INR800–900cr over time.

Sterlite Tech: Nuvama Report and my thoughts

Nuvama has come up with an updated report on Sterlite Tech with a price target of 770.

Their earlier price target was 440, which they increased to 770 after Q11FY27 results..
That's an upgrade of 75%
Just imagine the amount of earnings surprise.

Before Q1Fy27 results, many brokerages were expecting Sterlite to generate a PAT of 400-500 crores in FY27
Now, the same brokerages are estimating FY27 PAT to be 900-100 Crores, almost an increase of 100%

Nuvama report estimates Fy27 PAT of 906 Cr.
However, this is still conservative and below the management guidance  - Nuvama has considered EBITDA margins of 20.3% whereas Company has guided for 23%

Also, Sterlite recently did a QIP of 1500 Cr. While this will lead to a dilution of 5%, the entire debt is gone on one shot and it has become a net cash company !!

Personally, I think Sterlite would cross 1000 Cr PAT for FY 27 easily and might hit 1100 Cr.

Now, the interesting part - valuations
Before Q1FY27 results, Sterlite was trading at a trailing PE of 500+. Many people looked at screener PE, and shouted bubble !!
Now, PE has already dropped to 121
On FY27 basis - Sterlite is trading at a PE of 30-32
Half of the stocks in the Indian market are trading at higher valuations !!

Always consider forward earnings and valuations.
Particularly for turnaround cases like Sterlite, it is futile to look at trailing PE !!

GS on Syngene
Buy, TP cut to Rs 450

1Q sales declining 16% yoy (-11% vs GSe), primarily due to the ongoing impact of inventory correction in biologics manufacturing, as research business also reported minor degrowth.

Adj. EBITDA margin at 12% (-916bps vs. GSe), were impacted by lower GMs and operating deleverage.

Lower FY27-29E EPS estimates by upto 28% to factor in the Q1 miss

CITI on Balkrishna Ind 
Sell, TP Rs 2150

1Q significantly above estimates as volume growth surprised positively.

Despite weaker gross margin, higher operating leverage and fx tailwinds boosted profits.
Mgmt. outlook is positive on India across OHT as well as the new 2W/truck & bus tyres.

EU demand would be monitored given adverse weather trends (though 1Q volumes were healthy).

In US, there is strong headroom for growth, given duty has stabilized at 10%.

That said, geopolitical environment remains volatile, manifesting in logistics-related challenges and rising raw material costs.

Remain cautious on BKT’s foray into car, truck & bus and 2W tyres.

MS on Exide
OW, TP Rs 391

Posted 18% YoY revenue growth, revenues were 2% ahead of MSe
Low base, price hikes and strong growth across verticals excluding telecom drove growth.

High margin inverters segment, on a low base, would have also done well given strong summer demand.

Assuming core business at 18x FY28 P/E, investments at market price, then EESL implied price is 1x P/B.

Successful ramp up on EESL side is next driver for stock.

CITI on Exide
Buy, TP Rs 410

1Q significantly above estimates, driven by healthy revenue growth across segments.

Price-hikes and better mix helped offset the impact of higher commodity costs on gross margin.

Healthy operating leverage further helped EBITDA margin.

Mgmt. noted that demand continues to be strong across segments, driven by GST cuts.
Commodity cost pressures remain elevated

Still await more details on customer wins in the Li-ion business given the plant is now fully operational.

MOSL on Bajaj Fin
Upgrade to Buy, TP Rs 1300

Firing on all cylinders; a new earnings cycle begins
investment thesis is predicated on three structural pillars:

1) credit cycle has turned, which will enable lower credit costs and higher earnings

2) Multiple growth engines (core lending, digital ecosystem, gold loans, new businesses for BAF) are firing simultaneously

3) Duration and magnitude of this new earnings cycle leave room for both earnings upgrades & valuation support

Raise FY27/FY28 EPS estimates by 4%/2% to factor in higher AUM growth & lower credit costs

CLSA on Vedanta Aluminum
O-P, TP Rs 540

1Q largely in line, with Ebitda up 23% QoQ and COP falling US$20/t despite impact of Middle East conflict.

Key projects (capacity expansion guidance/coal and bauxite mine commissioning) were largely on track, which could drive US$175-200/t cost savings.

Net debt fell to Rs295bn (4Q: Rs330bn). VAML announced a dividend of Rs8/share

CITI on Vedanta Aluminum

Aluminium volumes rose 5% yoy/ 3% qoq to 632kt.

Vedanta Aluminium declared first interim dividend of Rs8/sh

MOSL on Torrent Pharma
Neutral, TP Rs 4730

Q1 better-than-expected, with 6%/9%/9% beat in revenue/EBITDA/PAT

Beat was due to higher growth in domestic branded formulation (DF) segment and stable growth momentum in US generics
Performance was dragged down to some extent by a muted show in Brazil and Germany

Currency tailwinds supported growth in these geographies in INR terms

TRP outperformed Indian Pharma market (IPM) by a wide margin (700bp), led by healthy growth in price, volume and new launches
Specifically, Curatio portfolio saw strong 34% YoY growth, partly driving overall DF growth for quarter.

HSBC on Torrent Pharma
Buy, TP Rs 5375

1Q another healthy quarter – base India sales (exJB Pharma) grew 19% y-o-y; JB Pharma sales recovered

Strong outlook for branded generics sales (mainly India) growth supports EBITDA margins growth

Approval and launch of semaglutide generic in Brazil next catalyst

GS on Piramal Pharma
Buy, TP Rs 250

Revenue/EBITDA grew by 17%/83% yoy, meaningfully above GSe/consensus driven by strong growth across all three segments
CDMO segment grew 19% yoy (+6% vs. GSe) as the CHG segment grew 17% yoy (+8% vs. GSe) and ICH grew 15% yoy (inline with GSe).

EBITDA margin came in at 8.6% (+308bps yoy, +135bps vs. GSe) driven by operating leverage.

After complete destocking in their largest CDMO product in FY26, note PPL reiterated (reckon they are on track to beat) their FY27 guidance of low to mid teen topline growth with EBITDA/PAT growth faster than topline growth, while also re-iterating their aspiration to reach revenues of US$2bn/25% EBITDA margin by FY30E
